data.description:
## Problem statement

The paid MunitoAI DeepSeek configuration lives only in the tracked
`.pi-config/agent` files and in this machine's `~/.pi/agent/models.json`, because
`scripts/install_pi.sh` merely copies those files **when the destination does not
already exist** — any established machine keeps its own (possibly drifted)
`models.json` and never receives the MunitoAI provider. The newer paid model
`deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is not configured at all, and no
DeepSeek/MunitoAI entry is in `enabledModels`, so paid DeepSeek cannot be reached
from the model cycle.

## Users

Framework operator (producer) on any machine that installs SorraAgents, and any
agent session that wants to run a paid DeepSeek model.

- As an operator, I want `scripts/install_pi.sh` to apply the tracked MunitoAI
  paid-DeepSeek provider to `~/.pi/agent/models.json` even when that file already
  exists, so every project on every machine gets the same model set without me
  hand-editing JSON.
- As an operator, I want the paid DeepSeek models in `enabledModels`, so I can
  reach them with `Ctrl+P` model cycling and as a startup selection.
- As an agent session, I want to select
  `MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` and have it answer, so paid
  DeepSeek is usable for real work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/models.json` exposes **both** paid MunitoAI DeepSeek
  models under one `MunitoAI` provider — `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`
  (existing) and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` (new) — with
  `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`; no credential is committed.
- [ ] `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` `enabledModels` contains `MunitoAI/*` and
  `deepseek/deepseek*` in addition to the existing `Local Proxy/plan` and
  `Local Proxy/code` entries.
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` merges the tracked `providers` (models and
  `modelOverrides` included) into an existing `~/.pi/agent/models.json` and
  unions the tracked `enabledModels` into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, instead
  of only copying when absent: no interactive prompt is required,
  **local-only providers/models/patterns are preserved**, and the run prints a
  per-provider summary (`Added …` / `OK: already present …`). Proven by an
  install run against a pre-populated sandboxed `$HOME` whose `models.json`
  lacks `MunitoAI` (today that run prints `Skipped …/models.json` and installs
  nothing).
- [ ] The merge is idempotent and non-destructive: a second run leaves both files
  semantically unchanged (no duplicated models, no lost local entries), a single
  timestamped `models.json.bak.<ts>` / `settings.json.bak.<ts>` backup is written
  before the first modification, writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and an
  unparseable existing JSON is reported and left untouched (fail-open, never
  half-written or overwritten).
- [ ] Post-install verification succeeds on a machine holding a valid MunitoAI
  credential: `pi --list-models munito` lists both MunitoAI DeepSeek models and
  `pi -p --no-tools --model MunitoAI/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017
  "reply with ok"` returns a response.
- [ ] Tests cover the merge helper and the install wiring (fresh install,
  pre-existing drifted file, idempotent re-run, local-only provider preserved,
  malformed JSON fail-safe) using a sandboxed `$HOME`; the new tests fail before
  the change and pass after it.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No credentials in the repository: keep `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"` env
  interpolation. The operator's stored `auth.json` credential (present on this
  machine) takes precedence over that env var at runtime.
- The merge must be non-destructive: it may add or refresh tracked providers, but
  must never drop a locally defined provider, model, `modelOverrides` entry or
  `enabledModels` pattern; write atomically (temp file + rename).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` must stay non-interactive-safe — the test harness runs
  it with `stdin=/dev/null`, where the current prompt degrades to `Skipped`.
- Keep existing install conventions: idempotent helpers, `create_symlink`
  backup-not-delete behaviour, fail-open warnings, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL`
  opt-out unaffected.
- MunitoAI publishes no context/pricing metadata (`GET /inference/v1/models`
  returns ids only), so `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` for the new model mirror the
  existing `…v4-flash` entry (400000 / 16384) and must be flagged as unverified
  in a code comment.
- Do not widen scope to other MunitoAI models (`zai-org/glm-5.3-flash`,
  `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, `munito/ocr-*`, …) — record them as follow-up work items if
  they become interesting.

## Existing state

- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` already contains a `MunitoAI` provider
  (`https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1`, `apiKey: "$MUNITOAI_API_KEY"`) with a
  single model `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` ("MunitoAI DeepSeek V4 Flash
  (paid)", 400000 / 16384, `input: ["text"]`). It arrived incidentally in
  `1ea3f20d3` ("chore: commit pre-existing working-tree leftovers before
  release"), untracked by any work item.
- `~/.pi/agent/models.json` on this machine is byte-identical to the tracked
  file and `pi --list-models munito` already lists
  `MunitoAI deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`.
- `GET https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/models` (queried with the stored
  credential) returns 11 ids, two of them DeepSeek:
  `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` and `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`.
  A live non-streaming call to `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` returned
  HTTP 200 with content `ok` plus a `reasoning` field.
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` (and the installed copy) has
  `enabledModels: ["Local Proxy/plan", "Local Proxy/code"]` — no DeepSeek or
  MunitoAI entry.
- **The install gap:** `scripts/install_pi.sh` uses
  `copy_if_missing_or_prompt` for `settings.json`/`models.json`. Reproduced
  against a sandboxed `$HOME` holding a pre-existing `models.json` without
  `MunitoAI`: the run prints `Skipped …/models.json` and the resulting file has
  no `MunitoAI` provider.
- `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` already holds a `MunitoAI` key (52 chars);
  `$MUNITOAI_API_KEY` is not set in the environment.

## Desired change

1. Add `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` to the tracked `MunitoAI` provider
   in `.pi-config/agent/models.json`, keeping the existing `…v4-flash` entry.
2. Add `MunitoAI/*` and `deepseek/deepseek*` to the tracked `enabledModels`.
3. Replace the consent-only whole-file copy in `scripts/install_pi.sh` with an
   idempotent, non-interactive **merge** of the tracked `providers` into
   `~/.pi/agent/models.json` plus a union merge of `enabledModels` into
   `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`; keep whole-file copy only for a missing
   destination. Back up before the first modification, write atomically, and fail
   open (warn, leave the file intact) on unparseable JSON.
4. Document the behaviour and the post-install verification commands.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — add the `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
  entry to the existing `MunitoAI` provider block.
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` — extend `enabledModels` with `MunitoAI/*` and
  `deepseek/deepseek*`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — replace `copy_if_missing_or_prompt` usage for
  `models.json`/`settings.json` with the merge step (keeping copy-if-missing for a
  fresh `$HOME`).
- `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` (new) — dependency-free (stdlib) idempotent
  JSON merge helper: provider/model refresh, `enabledModels` union, atomic write,
  timestamped backup, fail-open on invalid JSON; invoked by `install_pi.sh`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_models_config.py` (new) — sandboxed-`$HOME` install
  wiring: fresh install, pre-populated drifted config gains `MunitoAI`,
  local-only provider preserved, idempotent re-run, malformed JSON fail-safe.
- `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` (new) — unit tests for merge semantics,
  backup creation, atomicity, `enabledModels` union.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — document the global install's config merge
  behaviour and post-install verification (`pi --list-models munito`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** tracked values win for providers the tracked config defines
  (including a locally customised `MunitoAI` block); every *other* local
  provider/model/override is untouched.
- **Assumption (OPEN QUESTION):** `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is
  included because it is the newer paid DeepSeek model on the account; the
  operator's Q1 answer focused on installation and did not explicitly name it.
  Dropping it is a one-line revert.
- **Assumption:** `…v4.1-flash-1017` shares the existing `…v4-flash` limits
  (400000 / 16384). Unverified — MunitoAI publishes no metadata; a wrong value
  only mis-sizes pi's context accounting.
- **Risk (thinking metadata):** the new model returns a `reasoning` field, but
  whether the endpoint accepts reasoning-effort parameters is unverified;
  do not set `reasoning: true`/`thinkingFormat` without a streaming probe. Start
  by mirroring the existing entry; record a follow-up if tuning is needed.
- **Risk (local config clobbering):** a naive merge could drop an operator's
  bespoke provider or `modelOverrides`. Mitigation: preserve unknown providers
  verbatim, back up first, atomic rename, explicit test for the
  local-only-provider case.
- **Risk (auth mismatch):** `auth.json` wins over `$MUNITOAI_API_KEY`; a machine
  with neither sees the model as unavailable. Mitigation: keep the existing
  `pi login` reminder.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other MunitoAI models (GLM, Qwen, OCR) and DeepSeek
  provider tuning are tempting to bundle. Mitigation: out of scope; capture as
  linked follow-up items.
- **Risk (framework-wide blast radius):** every project runs
  `install_pi.sh`; a merge bug could corrupt `~/.pi/agent` config widely.
  Mitigation: fail-open on unparseable JSON, backup, atomic write, stdlib-only
  helper.

## Related work

- **SA-0MO4PG0U5004UJGP** — Add tracked .pi config and improve install_pi.sh to
  prompt for pi login (introduced the copy-if-missing/prompt install this item
  amends).
- **SA-0MQZXFKA9007FKU4** — Update pi-agent config: Local Proxy provider, model
  updates, version bump (precedent for editing tracked model config).
- **SA-0MTT7EUH30054I41** — Disable Pi auto-compaction for Local Proxy/plan
  (precedent for tracked `.pi-config/agent` changes with tests).
- Commits: `ebc5a1d7d` ("Add Deepseek" — direct DeepSeek provider),
  `1ea3f20d3` (introduced the `MunitoAI` provider block incidentally).
- **SA-0MW0GL4590046BTK** (this item).

### Automated find-related report

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (keyword-based, low signal here — the manual
list above is authoritative):

- **SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63** – Remote dev branch corrupted by test fixtures (test
  isolation bug) (completed)
- **SA-0MQZZ93110003MBU** – Add review of affected files in plan review stages
  (completed)
- **SA-0MUQ0I0YY000JCB5** – Remove stale references to missing .ralph.json and
  ralph config system (completed)
- Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `standups/2026_09_26.md` (keyword
  overlap only; not substantively related).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which MunitoAI deepseek model(s) should the config expose — (a) add
  `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` alongside the existing `…v4-flash`,
  (b) replace `…v4-flash`, (c) other?" — Answer (Map, interactive reply): "I see
  that we have a configuration in the local pi config. I want that config
  available to all projects using SorraAgents, the `./scripts/install_pi.sh`
  script should add it." → reframed the item: the tracked MunitoAI paid-DeepSeek
  config must be installed for every project/machine by `scripts/install_pi.sh`,
  not merely exist in the tracked file. Research: reproduced that
  `install_pi.sh` prints `Skipped …/models.json` when the destination already
  exists (sandboxed `$HOME`), so tracked config never lands on established
  machines.
- Q2: "Should the model be scoped into `enabledModels`? (a) add patterns,
  (b) leave untouched." — Answer (Map, interactive reply): "a - also add the
  `deepseek/deepseek*` model to `enabledModels`." → add `MunitoAI/*` **and**
  `deepseek/deepseek*` to the tracked `enabledModels`.
- Q3: "Does this work include applying the config locally and verifying it?" —
  Answer (Map, interactive reply): "see 1" → yes; installing via
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` and verifying selection/execution is in scope, hence
  the merge behaviour is an acceptance criterion.
- Q4 (agent research, no operator input needed): "Which DeepSeek ids does
  MunitoAI actually serve?" — Answer: `GET /inference/v1/models` with the stored
  credential returns `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` and
  `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`; a live call to the latter returned
  HTTP 200 (`content: "ok"`, plus `reasoning`).
- **OPEN QUESTION:** should `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` be added, or
  is `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` alone sufficient? Default taken: add both
  (newer paid model, additive, one-line revert). Context: operator's Q1 answer
  did not name the model explicitly.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-07: Plan decomposition complete (plan skill). 8 child work items created in test-first dependency order. AC coverage: 100% (`tree_coverage` recommendation: `proceed`). Key Files validated.
  1. **Update tracked models.json** (SA-0MW6RY8O1006M3F2) — add `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` to the MunitoAI provider.
  2. **Update tracked settings.json** (SA-0MW6RZ3AO0074UK6) — add `MunitoAI/*` and `deepseek/deepseek*` to `enabledModels`.
  3. **Unit tests for merge helper** (SA-0MW6S2MAL004U5KX) — test-first; no dependencies.
  4. **Create merge helper** (SA-0MW6S07QM005C6U2) — depends on the unit tests.
  5. **Integration tests for install wiring** (SA-0MW6S4NAQ001MAM1) — depends on merge helper and both data changes.
  6. **Update install_pi.sh** (SA-0MW6S1SEU005IDJ6) — depends on merge helper and integration tests.
  7. **Documentation** (SA-0MW6S4OSG008PYL1) — depends on merge helper and install script.
  8. **Verify post-install availability** (SA-0MW6SDDWD0008211) — depends on install script and both data changes.

## Plan: resolved ambiguities

- **"Flagged as unverified in a code comment"** — `models.json` is JSON and cannot carry comments. The unverified `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` flag for `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is recorded in the merge helper's docstring/constants (`scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py`) and in `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`. Resolution recorded in child SA-0MW6RY8O1006M3F2. If an in-file marker is required, a non-standard `//` comment would invalidate the JSON and is rejected.
- **OPEN QUESTION (carried forward): should `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` be added?** Default taken: add both models (newer paid model, purely additive, one-line revert if unwanted). Not blocking — implementation proceeds with the default; flagged here for producer awareness.

# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>   (historical reproduction in a sibling project)
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no

  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — the `code_freeze.py`

# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not widen the freeze semantics: this is a path-resolution fix, not a
  change to how a freeze is activated, cleared, or enforced.
- Keep the existing public API (`code_freeze_marker_path`, marker read/write
  helpers) and their `project_root` behaviour unchanged.
- Prefer re-using the shared helper over a second walk; if that would create a
  circular import, mirror the rule and reference the canonical one in a
  comment.
- Gate order: build → test → commit; no ad-hoc `pytest` — run tests through the
  test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake of the parent item)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 48) order:
  explicit `project_root` → `<cwd>/.worklog` → `<git toplevel>/.worklog` →
  `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`, each gated on `is_dir()` only.
- `code_freeze_marker_path()` (~line 90) uses that helper and falls back to
  `<cwd>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` when nothing resolves.
- The same candidate-construction defect is proven in
  `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` (parent item
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB`, AC1–AC3) — this item is the same rule applied to the
  code-freeze copy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/code_freeze.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` / marker path
  resolution (~lines 48–101).
- `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` — new worktree-layout cases
  (AC1–AC3).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — one sentence alongside the
  `StatusLifecycle` resolution note (if the rule is shared).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the shared helper is exported
  for reuse (no behaviour change expected here).

## Related work

- `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` — parent fix for `status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()`
  / `worklog_dir_flag()` (same rule, `wl`-facing seam). This item should land
  after it so the shared rule exists.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`, `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine) —
  discovery chain for the original defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: freeze bypass stays latent** until this item is implemented, if the
  parent fix lands alone. Mitigation: the parent item's docs state the
  code-freeze copy is still defective and link here.
- **Risk: duplicated rule drifts again.** Mitigation: AC4 prefers the shared
  helper.
- **Scope-creep risk:** touching freeze activation/enforcement or adding new
  marker features — out of scope; record such ideas as separate items.
- **Assumption:** the implement workflow's freeze check is the only consumer of
  `code_freeze_marker_path()`; verified by grep during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Fold this into the parent `worklog_dir_flag` fix?**
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — filed here; the parent item stays
  narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`, relayed via
  `SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (Appendix Q2).

## Goal

Investigate, and then reduce, large tool-call results before they enter conversation history, so that a single oversized tool result does not inflate every subsequent model turn. Prefer the cheapest effective mechanism; a small-model compaction call is one candidate among several.

## Evidence (from the proxy incident 2026-11-03, LLM repo)

- A single tool-role message of 51,945 bytes (a full SKILL.md pasted into history by the audit skill) entered the conversation at 08:41:54. The conversation grew from 22 KB to 120 KB of content over 7 turns, and the prompt went 6,564 to 33,570 tokens.
- Every subsequent turn re-prefilled the growing tail on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte.
- The proxy priced that 51,945-byte append at 173 new tokens against a measured 12,936 (deficit_ratio 0.659), so the cost was invisible to admission control as well as to the agent.
- Session recordings and session jsonl files are available for measurement: ~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/ and ~/.pi/agent/sessions/.

## Candidate approaches, cheapest first

1. Measure first: rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions to identify which tools dominate (skill-body pastes, wl show --json dumps, file reads). Deterministic script, no model call.
2. Truncate with re-read: a Pi extension intercepts a tool result above a threshold, keeps head and tail plus an explicit "truncated N bytes, re-read with offset/limit" marker, and preserves the raw output on disk.
3. Reference instead of inline: content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files) and substitute a short handle plus preview when the content is already in the prompt.
4. Small-model compaction at the boundary: the extension detects an oversized tool result and asks a small/fast model to compact only what the current request needs, prefixing the tool output with a purpose-built instruction. Must reuse the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1, as pinned by the proxy compaction_summarizer) so it does not contend with the main model, and must only escalate here when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient, since it is a model call on the critical path.
5. Structured projections at the tool level: JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, and flags that keep payloads small at source.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. Measured saving: avoiding 13k prefill tokens saves roughly 45-90 s at observed rates, so a ~2 s small-model call is a clear win; the strategy must be justified against that budget.
- It must not lose information the agent later needs, and any lossy step must be recoverable (raw payload retained and re-readable).
- It runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects, so it competes for capacity -- another reason to prefer non-model approaches first.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot, is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in SorraAgents

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, worklog-post-pull

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/` (or the existing test-skill test location) — regression test for a stale-base fixture.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document the returned-value contract if it is described there.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).

## Summary

Refactor duplicate prevention is a **substring match over other items' titles and descriptions**, keyed on file + line + rule code. It silently fails whenever the line number moves by one, whenever the path prefix differs (worktree vs main checkout), or whenever the title has been truncated — so the same smell is re-filed on every scan.

## Evidence

Function: `_has_existing_worklog_item()` in `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`. It lists `wl list --tags Refactor --json`, concatenates each item's title and description, and returns a match only when **all three** of `target_file`, `target_code` and `str(target_line)` appear anywhere in that blob.

Open-backlog duplicates measured on 2026-11-08:

| Target | Rule | Open items for the same file+rule |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` | `S112` | 22 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` | `SIM117` | 10 |
| `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` | `ISC004` | 7 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_temp_index.py` | `SIM117` | 4 |
| `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` | `RUF015` | 4 |

Failure modes that defeat the guard:

1. **Line drift** — inserting one line above a finding changes every subsequent line number, so `str(target_line) in combined` no longer matches.
2. **Path-prefix drift** — the identical file is recorded as `/repo/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill/x.py` from one scan and `/repo/skill/x.py` from another; neither is a substring of the other.
3. **Truncation** — titles are truncated in listing output (e.g. `[MEDIUM] /home/…/test_implement_push_fro`), so the full path is not present to match on.
4. **Cross-family blindness** — the guard only inspects `Refactor`-tagged items, so the audit-side family `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (73 open items, created by `audit_runner.py`) is invisible to it and mints parallel twins for the same diagnostics.

Note also that a substring match on a *line number* is not an identity: `str(12)` matches `:12`, `:120`, `:312`, and any mention of 12 anywhere in a long description.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Identity for a refactor finding is `(repository-relative path, rule/smell code)` — **not** the line number, and not the absolute path. The content fingerprint required by the re-verification item (`SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`) is stored alongside it so occurrences can be counted rather than guessed at.
2. Before creating an item the skill queries the existing open items for that exact identity **and** for the audit-created `ruff <RULE> in <path>` family, so the two producers cannot mint twins.
3. A repeat finding on an existing identity does not create a new item: it appends a comment recording the new line numbers/occurrences, or updates the existing item, per a documented rule.
4. Worktree path prefixes are normalised before comparison (shared helper, reused by the critical bug on worktree-path recording).
5. Line-level reporting is preserved: the item lists every affected line, so consolidation loses no diagnostic detail.
6. Regression tests covering: same smell twice in one run; smell re-found after a line shift; same file scanned from two worktrees; two different rules in one file; refactor-created vs audit-created twin suppression.
7. A one-off consolidation of the existing duplicates is possible from the same helper (dry-run first), so the backlog can be collapsed without manual wl calls.

## Related

- Critical bug `SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2`: refactor filings record ephemeral implement-worktree paths (the path-drift half of this problem; the shared path-normalisation helper is specified there and reused here).
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`: linter-derived items are never re-verified — supplies the content fingerprint and the occurrence re-check.
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS`: children survive parent deletion — the orphan half of the same backlog-hygiene gap.

## Impact

The same code smell is tracked once instead of up to twenty-two times, so the backlog reflects genuine debt and agents stop re-fixing work that is already queued.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD** – Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines, evaluate refactor need, and file work items (open)
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** – Fix legacy skill/ path reference in planall SKILL.md (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absolute, acceptance, affected, agents, alongside (+191 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: absolute, acceptance, affected, agents, alongside (+181 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absolute, acceptance, affected, agents, alongside (+176 more)


## Plan: changelog (2026-11-12)

Planned by the `plan` skill (session via herdr-downtime dispatch):

- Computed effort/risk estimate (Small/Medium, 74% confidence) via the effort-and-risk skill; stored on the item and recorded as a comment.

# `finish` cannot converge after an interrupted push: a prior-run commit is not attributed

## Problem statement

SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 made `finish` refuse the terminal write when its run creates no commit (AC1). The refusal triggers on `CommitOutcome.committed` being false — i.e. **only commits created by the current run count**.

That misses the documented interruption-recovery contract in `phase_finish`'s own docstring (SA-0MVXUSJJY009HMQ0): "Re-running `finish` then converges to `completed` / `in_review` through the ordinary no-diff/no-op-push path." After an interrupted push the worktree is **clean** and its commit already exists, so a re-run creates no commit and is now refused with `commit.reason = "no_commit_no_signal"` — a message that also states, falsely, that "nothing was committed or pushed".

Observed (2026-11-09): SA-0MW74IKJE008JXDQ's session timed out during the dev push. Commit `049ff2669` existed on the worktree branch and on local `dev` but not on `origin/dev`; `finish` could not be re-run to publish and finalise it. The work had to be pushed and reconciled by hand.

Parent AC2 already scopes attribution correctly — a report "may only name a commit that is attributable to this item (created by this finish run **or a prior run of this item's worktree**)" — so this is the missing half of that requirement, not new scope.

## Users

- Agent sessions running `implement.py finish` that were interrupted during the push phase, which must now be recovered without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `phase_finish` attributes a commit created by a **prior run of this item's worktree**: when `git_commit` reports no new commit but HEAD carries commits that are ahead of the parent branch (`origin/<parent_branch>`) and whose messages reference the work-item id, finish proceeds with the existing fast-forward/push path, names that commit in the report, the completion comment and the retained-state interruption record (`_set_finish_progress`), and finalises normally.
- AC2 — The refusal still fires for a genuinely work-less worktree: no attributable commit ahead of the parent branch and no verification-only signal → `commit.reason = "no_commit_no_signal"`, no terminal write, no push, no completion comment (the parent epic's AC1).
- AC3 — The no-op refusal message no longer claims "nothing was committed or pushed" when an attributable commit exists but is not being attributed; wording is accurate for both paths.
- AC4 — Automated regression coverage: (i) an interrupted-push re-run (clean tree, attributable commit ahead of `origin/dev`, absent from `origin/dev`) converges to `completed`/`in_review` and publishes the commit; (ii) the existing no-work refusal test still fails loudly; (iii) `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` exercises the **real** `git_commit` boundary (not a truthy stub) for the converging re-run, so the stub can no longer mask this path.
- AC5 — `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` state that a re-run after an interrupted push finalises by attributing the prior-run commit.

## Impact

A finish interrupted during its push can be re-run to completion instead of being refused as a no-op, so an agent never has to push and reconcile a half-finished item by hand.

## Constraints

- Attribution must be strict: only commits whose messages reference the work-item id and that are attributable to this worktree are considered. Ambient HEAD from another item's commit must never be claimed (parent epic AC2).
- The refusal path must remain intact for genuinely work-less items.
- The fix must not change the behaviour when `git_commit` succeeds (creates a new commit).

## Existing state

`phase_finish` (commit-outcome branch, ~line 11900 of `implement.py`; line numbers as of this plan) checks `commit_outcome.committed`. When `False`, it:
1. Sets `commit_hash = git_get_commit_hash(worktree_path)` (ambient HEAD — discarded from the report)
2. Sets `reason = "no_commit_no_signal"`
3. Refuses the terminal write with a message that says "nothing was committed or pushed"

The code at ~line 11969 sets `_set_finish_progress` with `commit=""` (never attributes the ambient HEAD), confirming the design intent to not misattribute. But it also never looks for an attributable commit from a prior run.

## Desired change

When `commit_created` is False in `phase_finish`:
1. Check whether HEAD of the worktree has commits ahead of the parent branch whose messages reference the work-item id.
2. If an attributable commit is found, use it for the report and push path (proceed as if committed).
3. If not, refuse with an updated message that does not falsely claim "nothing was committed or pushed".

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-10)

Effort **Small**, risk **Low** — below the decomposition threshold, so no child
work items: this is one end-to-end slice.

**Implementation order (test-first).**

1. Extend `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` with the
   interrupted-push re-run case driven through the **real** `git_commit`
   boundary: a temporary repository whose worktree is clean, whose HEAD is one
   commit ahead of `origin/dev` with a message referencing the item id, and
   which is absent from `origin/dev`. It must fail before the fix (AC4 i/iii).
2. Attribute the prior-run commit in `phase_finish` and correct the refusal
   wording (AC1/AC3); the `--verification-only` path stays untouched.
3. Confirm `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` still fails
   loudly on a genuinely work-less worktree (AC2/AC4 ii).
4. Update `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
   (AC5).

**Reuse.** `_classify_child_worktree` (~line 2097) already carries the exact
attribution shape AC1 needs — `git rev-list --count <base>..HEAD`, then
`git log <base>..HEAD --grep <item-id> -n 1 --format=%H`. Share that as a
helper rather than reimplementing it, with one crucial difference in the base:
AC1 compares against `origin/<parent_branch>`, not local `<parent_branch>` —
after an interrupted push the commit is already on *local* `dev`, so a
local-`dev` base reports "0 ahead" and would re-refuse. Attribution stays
strict: no `--grep` match → no attribution (parent epic AC2).

**Duplicate check.** Searched `no_commit_no_signal`, `prior-run commit` and
`attributable commit`: SA-0MW74IJWI009NRZ1 (completed) scopes only the
refusal, and parent epic SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 explicitly leaves this half out.
No item satisfies these ACs; no duplicate created or closed.

**Vertical slice.** A single slice through code + tests + docs; phasing is
unnecessary here and deliberately not applied.

**Plan: changelog (2026-11-10).** AC1 now names the retained-state
interruption record alongside the report and completion comment (the
`_set_finish_progress` call is the third place the description's "Existing
state" flags as never attributing). Stale line anchors refreshed; Plan block
added with test-first order, the reuse note (including the
`origin/<parent_branch>` base caveat) and the duplicate-check result. No AC
was added, removed or re-scoped; no child items were created.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` commit-outcome branch (~line 11580), `git_get_commit_hash`, the refusal message, `_set_finish_progress`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` — new test for the interrupted-push re-run convergence
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — ensure existing no-work refusal test still passes
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the re-run attribution behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document the re-run attribution behaviour

## Related work

- SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 — Parent epic: "Finish must not mark an item terminal when its worktree produced no commit and its ACs need an operational run"
- SA-0MVXUSJJY009HMQ0 — Interruption recovery: the documented contract this fix enables
- SA-0MW74IJWI009NRZ1 — The refusal slice that introduced the gap (SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 child)
- SA-0MW74IKJE008JXDQ — The observed live incident: timed-out session with unpushed commit

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

None — the work item was already sufficiently defined with clear ACs, key files, and an existing bug report. All acceptance criteria are testable and measurable.

- Q: none directed to the producer — planning auto-skipped the interview
  (effort Small / risk Low) and no question was needed.
  Research note (plan, 2026-11-10): `_classify_child_worktree`
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:2097`) already implements the
  `<base>..HEAD` + `--grep <item-id>` attribution pattern AC1 needs. AC1 must
  use `origin/<parent_branch>` as its base because after an interrupted push
  the commit is already on local `dev`. Source: code inspection of
  `implement.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py`.
- Review evidence (plan, 2026-11-10): all five predicted key files exist and
  pass `validate_key_files_format()`; the AC section parses to exactly 5 ACs.

# Bug — a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files

discovered-from:SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40 (driving the parent AC4 test gap exposed it).

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection()` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) resolves a
declared test **group** first and returns immediately:

```python
group_name = select_group_from_changed_files(changed, root)
if group_name is not None:
    group_cmds = group_commands(group_name, root)
    if group_cmds:
        return ChangedScopeSelection(list(group_cmds), ...)
```

When a change set touches **both** a path matched by a group (`paths`) and a
test file the group does not cover, the group's command replaces the file-level
selection instead of unioning with it. The edit-authored test file is then
silently absent from the changed-scope run.

### Observed (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40)

Changed files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` → matches the `implement` group
  (`skill/implement/**`) → command `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings
  skill/implement/tests/`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` (the file the run was verifying) → **dropped**

Result: `212 passed`, none of them the two newly added tests. Running with only
the test file changed selected it correctly (`212 passed` including the new
tests), so the loss is specific to the group short-circuit.

## Impact

A red-witness / green-evidence run can report success while never executing the
tests the author just wrote, so the implement `finish` gate and any other
changed-scope consumer under-report. The dev-push full-suite gate is the only
backstop.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A selection where a group matches *and* other changed test files exist emits
   the group's commands **unioned** with the file-level selection (deduplicated,
   deterministic order), or fails closed to the full suite — never silently
   drops a changed test file.
2. A test pins the union (changed source under a group path + changed test file
   outside the group's directories); the emitted command lists both.
3. A test pins that a group-only match still emits exactly the group command
   (no behaviour change for the single-match case).
4. `run_tests.py --scope changed` on a change set containing
   `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` + `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
   selects `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.
5. Changed-scope tests pass; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.


## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `changed_scope_selection()` short-circuits
  on a matched group (the bug); `select_group_from_changed_files()` picks the
  group; `_commands_for_selected_tests()` builds the file-level commands and
  `group_commands()` resolves the group's declared commands.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — changed-scope selection tests
  (`TestChangedScopeGroups`); the union + group-only regression tests (AC2/AC3)
  belong here.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_run_group_from_changed_files()` is
  a second, redundant group-first short-circuit: `_run_resolved_suite()` returns
  its result before `changed_scope_selection()` is consulted. See OPEN QUESTION.

## Test-first ordering

Write the failing union tests (AC2/AC3) first and confirm they reproduce the
drop against the current `changed_scope_selection()`, then fix. After the fix
the changed-scope run (AC4) must list `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.

## Suggested approach

1. In `changed_scope_selection()`, when a group matches, also resolve the
   file-level selection for changed test files **not** covered by the matched
   group's `paths`, then return the union: group commands first (declared
   order), then file-level commands (sorted), deduplicated. Keep the
   single-match (group-only) case byte-identical (AC3).
2. If the union cannot be constructed safely, fail closed to the full suite
   rather than dropping a changed test file (AC1).

## OPEN QUESTION

Is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_run_group_from_changed_files()` in
scope for this item, or deferred to SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9 (changed-scope group
union + selector convergence, AC3)?

- Why it matters: fixing only `changed_scope_selection()` leaves the implement

## Summary

Replace the substring-based dedupe (_has_existing_worklog_item) with an exact, line-independent identity for refactor-filed smells (parent SA-0MW7Z1AU1006UT9C). A finding's identity is (repository-relative path, rule/smell code) — never the line number, never an absolute path — carried in a machine-readable marker in the item description so lookups survive line drift, worktree-path drift and title truncation.

## Key Files

- skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py — identity helper, marker emission, _has_existing_worklog_item replacement
- skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py — batch grouping so same-identity smells file one item
- tests/test_refactor/test_workitem_creation.py, tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py — F1 suite

## Target outcome

Every refactor item carries a stable identity + fingerprint, and the pre-creation guard matches on exact identity instead of substrings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Identity of a finding is (repo-relative path, rule/smell code); line number and absolute path are excluded. Paths are normalised with the existing shared _repo_relative_path helper from SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2 (worktree prefixes stripped).
- New items embed the identity as a machine-readable marker (Refactor-Finding-Key: <code>:<path>), a content fingerprint (Refactor-Fingerprint: sha256 of target-file content + rule set, per AC1 of the re-verification item SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3), and the full affected-line list (Refactor-Affected-Lines: n, m) so consolidation loses no diagnostic detail (AC5).
- _has_existing_worklog_item is replaced by an exact-key lookup: one "wl list Refactor-Finding-Key: --json" call, local regex parse (audit-side CFP-Chore-Key precedent), filter to non-terminal items only, exact key comparison after path normalisation — no substring matching anywhere.
- Batch creation (create_smell_work_items) groups same-identity findings into one item whose affected-line list is the union (covers parent AC6 case 1: same smell twice in one run; AC5 line-level reporting).
- The F1 regression suite for identity, markers, fingerprint and normalisation passes.
- skill/refactor/SKILL.md documents the identity definition, marker format, and fingerprint semantics.

## Constraints

- Identity must remain stable when the same file is scanned from an implement worktree and from the main checkout (reuse _repo_relative_path; do not duplicate it).
- Marker must sit near the top of the description so truncation cannot hide it; wl list --json returns full descriptions (verified).

## Risky assumptions

- Files whose path contains a colon are out of scope (matches the audit-side CFP-Chore-Key precedent); documented in SKILL.md.
- Fingerprint schema: sha256 of file bytes + rule code at filing time; may need to align exactly with SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3 when that item lands — the marker is additive and will be consumed there.

## Impact

Duplicate filings stop: the same smell collapses to one tracked item with all its lines, regardless of which worktree or scan produced it.

data.description:
## Problem Statement

The ship release changelog generator (`generate-changelog.js` in the ship skill) queries `stage: in_review` work items with `execSync` using the **default 1 MB `maxBuffer`**. The jq projection includes each item's **full description** (`{id, title, issueType, description, parentId}`). When the in_review set at release time is large enough that the projected JSON exceeds 1 MB, Node's execSync kills the stream with `ENOBUFS`, the bare `catch {}` swallows the exception and logs the misleading `Warning: could not query completed/in_review work items (wl not available?)`, and the generator returns `[]`.

Result (observed in the v1.0.29 ContextHub release, 2026-11-12): the CHANGELOG section for v1.0.29 was created empty (header only), and the Discord release notification contained no changelog. The release itself succeeded (non-fatal by design), and the section had to be rebuilt manually afterwards.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** running `/skill:ship release` — they expect every release to ship a populated changelog and a Discord notification containing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Explicit maxBuffer:** the `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` execSync in `generate-changelog.js` sets a `maxBuffer` large enough to hold the full projected JSON (e.g. 64 MB), so a large in_review backlog never trips `ENOBUFS`.
2. **Bounded output (defence in depth):** the jq projection no longer pipes unbounded full descriptions through the execSync buffer — **decided: project skinny fields `{id, title, issueType, parentId}` and fetch descriptions lazily** for the parent items that survive `getParentsOnly()` — so output size is bounded regardless of backlog size.
3. **Real error surfaced:** the `catch {}` block logs the actual `err.message`/`err.code` (e.g. ENOBUFS) instead of the misleading "wl not available?" warning.
4. **Regression test:** a test reproduces the large-output scenario (e.g. 1 MB+ projection) and asserts the generator returns the full item set rather than `[]`.
5. **Positive check (optional but recommended):** when the query legitimately returns 0 in_review items, the generator logs a loud warning that an empty changelog will be produced.

## Constraints

- Changelog generation must remain non-fatal to the release (a failed generation continues with a warning), but a *silent empty section* must not occur.
- Do not modify the release gate behaviour (audit/final-validation gates are unaffected by this change).
- Lazy description fetching must **not** re-introduce an unbounded buffer: fetch per item (or in small bounded batches) through a helper with its own explicit `maxBuffer`, and degrade to a title-only entry when a single fetch fails.

## Existing State

- Root cause reproduced: running the exact generator command against a large stage (`wl list --stage done --json | jq -c "[.workItems[] | {id, title, issueType, description, parentId}]"`) throws `spawnSync /bin/sh ENOBUFS` with default maxBuffer (10.5 MB output for 3,025 items).
- v1.0.29 (ContextHub) shipped an empty changelog section; the section was manually rebuilt after the fact.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` — `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` (skinny jq projection + explicit `maxBuffer`), new lazy description-fetch helper, and the `catch {}` error-surfacing fix in the same function.
- `tests/unit/test-generate-changelog-query.mjs` — extend with the large-description regression test (1 MB+ projection) and the skinny-projection/lazy-fetch contract.
- `tests/node/test-generate-changelog.mjs` — end-to-end coverage of categorisation still receiving descriptions for parent items.

## Related Work

- Ship skill SKILL.md documents changelog generation as non-fatal (release proceeds on failure).
- Two completed items in ContextHub describe a related-but-distinct `wl list --stage in_review` rendering parity bug (not the cause here).
- SA-0MSLW5P7J0068UFZ — ship: replace dual wl list queries with single AND query + jq projection (completed; fixed the dual-query union but not the description-size issue).
- SA-0MRC71KCR009Y7RL — Generate CHANGELOG.md during ship release process (completed).
- SA-0MRGKZ3QY003498O — Intake and plan skills should not require CHANGELOG.md updates — handled by ship skill (completed).

## Open Questions

None — the AC2 approach question is resolved (Option A: skinny projection + lazy description fetch).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- Q: "Which bounded-output approach is preferred for AC2 — (A) skinny jq projection + lazy description fetch, or (B) keep the current projection and raise `maxBuffer` to 64 MB?" — Answer (producer): **Option A — project `{id, title, issueType, parentId}` only and fetch descriptions lazily.** Source: interactive reply in the intake session. Prior answer: none (first answer). Research: `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` currently projects `description` for every in_review item (`generate-changelog.js`); `getParentsOnly()` already narrows to parent items before categorisation, so lazy fetching only applies to a small subset — making Option A's extra calls bounded and cheap.
data.title: Changelog generator silently emits empty release section when in_review set exceeds execSync maxBuffer

**AC1** — Explicit maxBuffer:
- Set `maxBuffer` on the `execSync` call in `getCompletedOrInReviewItems()` to a large value (e.g. 64 MB) as a safety net.

**AC2** — Skinny jq projection:
- Remove `description` from the jq projection: change from `{id, title, issueType, description, parentId}` to `{id, title, issueType, parentId}`.
- This ensures output size is bounded regardless of backlog size.

**AC3** — Real error surfaced:
- Replace the bare `catch {}` with one that logs the actual `err.message`/`err.code` (e.g. ENOBUFS) instead of the misleading "wl not available?" warning.

## Goal
Create the Python wrapper script (`run_mutation.py`) that:

3. Invokes Stryker (via `npx` or a local install)
4. Parses the JSON report and extracts per-module mutation scores

- [ ] `skill/mutation-test/scripts/run_mutation.py` resolves project root from `--project-root` argument.
- [ ] Config merging: base Stryker config + scope overrides (mutate paths) per module.
- [ ] Runtime enforcement: a wall-clock timer per module; if exceeded, emit budget-breach flag + partial report.
- [ ] JSON report parsing: extract mutation scores, killed/survived/equivalent mutant counts, runtime.
